The frozen ocean application contains 200 distinct North Pacific profiles.
Silicate is the response; salinity and log pressure are fully observed.
Oxygen is recorded through four bands (boundaries 50, 100, 150 µmol/kg),
with 0%, 20%, or 50% exact training measurements. The same five folds and
nested measurement masks are used throughout.

## 1. Choose the work

The default is **paper/plan**, which checks the design and displays selected
tasks without fitting. Set `action: "run"` to execute selected tasks, or
`action: "report"` to read available results. A report can be partial;
each score group shows its completed fold count.

| Selector | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `modules` | Choose initial EIV fits, original baselines, continuation, expanded baselines, prediction reporting, diagnostics, or surface displays |
| `folds`, `cells` | Choose training folds and calibration cases; reporting reads all available outputs |
| `augmented_methods`, `placeholders` | Choose expanded baseline methods and predeclared b values |
| `task_ids` | Optional exact task selection, within the other selectors |
| `output_dir`, `run_id` | Separate device results and identify this execution's logs |
| `import_dirs` | Compatible result roots to merge before running/reporting |

Each machine should use its own result directory. For example, one machine
can run folds 1–3 and the other folds 4–5. Transfer their result directories,
then render with `action="report"`, a fresh output directory, and both roots
in `import_dirs`. The merger checks input, code, package, and task provenance,
and refuses conflicting payloads. Runnable examples are in
`codes/applications/ocean_silicate/README.md`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE,message=FALSE,warning=TRUE,cache=FALSE,error=FALSE)
input <- knitr::current_input(dir=TRUE)
repository_dir <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(input),".."),mustWork=TRUE)
source(file.path(repository_dir,"codes/applications/ocean_silicate/01_setup.R"),local=TRUE)
ocean_source_modules(repository_dir,environment())
settings <- ocean_settings(profile=params$profile,action=params$action,folds=params$folds,
  cells=params$cells,modules=params$modules,augmented_methods=params$augmented_methods,
  placeholders=params$placeholders,task_ids=params$task_ids,cores=params$cores,run_id=params$run_id)
data_dir <- if(nzchar(params$data_dir)) ocean_resolve_path(params$data_dir,repository_dir) else file.path(repository_dir,"data/ocean_silicate")
output_dir <- if(nzchar(params$output_dir)) ocean_resolve_path(params$output_dir,repository_dir) else file.path(repository_dir,"reproduction/ocean",settings$profile)
diagnostics_dir <- if(nzchar(params$diagnostics_dir)) ocean_resolve_path(params$diagnostics_dir,repository_dir) else file.path(output_dir,"diagnostics")
import_dirs <- as.character(unlist(params$import_dirs)); import_dirs <- import_dirs[nzchar(import_dirs)]
import_dirs <- ocean_resolve_path(import_dirs,repository_dir)
augmented_output_dir <- if(nzchar(params$augmented_output_dir)) ocean_resolve_path(params$augmented_output_dir,repository_dir) else ""
```

```{r task-plan, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(profile=settings$profile,action=settings$action,
  chains=settings$chains,iterations=settings$iter,burn=settings$burn,cores=settings$cores))
knitr::kable(ocean_select_tasks(settings))
```

Paper EIV fits use four chains × 20,000 iterations, burn-in 5,000, and
`u_block_size=8`. Each cell is screened using its own initial-chain results.
If the maximum finite Rhat exceeds 1.01 or the minimum finite bulk ESS is
below 400 (or no finite values exist), its saved chains receive one additional
20,000 iterations. The rule is fixed before fitting; no fold/cell list is fixed.
Undefined diagnostics and tail ESS are recorded for review. This limited
screen is not a full convergence assessment. After the one permitted extension,
remaining screen failures are reported for review, without an automatic loop.
Continuation restores saved RNG states and requires only its own initial fit.
The main study has 50 base tasks plus the number of diagnostic-selected
continuations; the task plan includes all 15 conditional candidates.
The optional `quick` profile runs fold 1/O0/O50 with one chain × 80 iterations;
it is a workflow check, not a paper comparison.

### Package calls in the fitting module

`02_fit_models.R` contains the numerical steps: `run_eiv()` prepares X, C
and an `U_obs` matrix (NA outside the fixed calibration mask), fits EIV-GP,
predicts held-out Y, and imputes hidden training U. `run_one()` continues
saved chains for cells selected by the current initial diagnostics. The following snippets are read
from the **actual executing script**; displaying them does not fit a second model.
Iterations, burn-in, chain count and seeds use the settings and task listed above.

```{r package-calls, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
fit_source <- readLines(file.path(repository_dir,"codes/applications/ocean_silicate/02_fit_models.R"))
show_package_call <- function(id, title) {
  start <- which(trimws(fit_source)==paste("# RMD-BEGIN",id))
  end <- which(trimws(fit_source)==paste("# RMD-END",id))
  stopifnot(length(start)==1L,length(end)==1L,end>start+1L)
  lines <- fit_source[seq.int(start+1L,end-1L)]
  indent <- min(nchar(lines)-nchar(sub("^ *","",lines)))
  lines <- substring(lines,indent+1L)
  cat("\n\n**",title,"**\n\n",sep="")
  child <- c(paste0("```{r call-",id,", eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, code_folding='show'}"),lines,"```")
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text=child,quiet=TRUE),sep="\n")
}
show_package_call("eiv-fit","1. Fit EIV-GP with partial exact oxygen")
show_package_call("eiv-predict","2. Predict Y from class-only test inputs")
show_package_call("eiv-impute","3. Impute hidden training oxygen (O20/O50)")
show_package_call("eiv-continue","4. Continue chains when the initial diagnostic screen fails")
show_package_call("native-baselines","5. Fit and predict native baselines with expanded inputs")
```

For mixed testing, `predict_eivgp(new_U=..., new_U_scale="raw")` replaces
predictions only at the saved exact-U test rows; other rows keep the
class-only predictions. At O0, `impute_eivgp(scale="model")` is used.

The baseline snippet uses the package's pinned internal adapter
(`:::`), which fits and predicts with the native functions below.
Original baselines use the same adapter with `m_vec=4`, continuous
X=(salinity, log pressure) and categorical C=oxygen class. Expanded
baselines use `m_vec=c(4,2)`, X=(salinity, log pressure, W) and
C=(oxygen class, R). Optimizer controls are specified in the fitting script.

| Method | Native fitting | Native prediction |
|---|---|---|
| UC-GP | `kergp::gp` with `kGauss` × `q1Symm` | `stats::predict` |
| LVGP | `LVGP::LVGP_fit` | `LVGP::LVGP_predict` |
| EzGP | `EzGP::EzGP_fit`, training-only nugget CV | `EzGP::EzGP_predict` |

`ocean_execute()` below selects/resumes these tasks and records logs and
receipts. Reporting reads their saved outputs; the fit calls above are
executed only for selected, unfinished tasks when `action="run"`.

```{r execute, include=FALSE}
analysis <- if(settings$action=="plan") ocean_execute(repository_dir,data_dir,output_dir,settings) else
  ocean_logged(file.path(output_dir,"jobs",settings$run_id,"execution.log"),
    ocean_execute(repository_dir,data_dir,output_dir,settings,
      import_dirs=import_dirs,augmented_output_dir=augmented_output_dir))
```

```{r continuation-decisions, eval=settings$action!="plan", echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(analysis$continuation_decisions[,c("fold","cell","max_rhat","min_ess_bulk",
  "n_nonfinite_rhat","n_nonfinite_ess_tail","decision")],digits=3)
final_fit_status<-ocean_final_eiv_sources(output_dir,settings$profile)
knitr::kable(final_fit_status[,c("fold","cell","continued","available","final_screen_pass")])
if(settings$profile=="paper" && any(final_fit_status$available & !final_fit_status$final_screen_pass,na.rm=TRUE))
  cat("Some final fits remain outside the limited screen; inspect chain diagnostics before treating the analysis as finalized.\n")
```

## 2. Observed data

Measured oxygen is retained in the source files for offline evaluation.
Only the fixed calibration rows supply exact training oxygen to the models.

```{r data-design, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(analysis$inputs$audit,digits=3)
```

```{r original-scatter, eval=settings$action!="plan", fig.width=11, fig.height=3.7}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
cohort <- analysis$inputs$cohort
p1 <- ggplot(cohort,aes(U,Y,color=oxygen_class))+geom_point(alpha=.65)+
  labs(x="Measured oxygen (micromol/kg)",y="Silicate (micromol/kg)")+theme_minimal()+theme(legend.position="none")
p2 <- ggplot(cohort,aes(G2salinity,Y,color=oxygen_class))+geom_point(alpha=.65)+
  labs(x="Salinity",y="Silicate (micromol/kg)")+theme_minimal()+theme(legend.position="none")
p3 <- ggplot(cohort,aes(G2pressure,Y,color=oxygen_class))+geom_point(alpha=.65)+
  labs(x="Pressure (dbar)",y="Silicate (micromol/kg)",color="Oxygen class")+theme_minimal()
p1+p2+p3
```

## 3. Held-out prediction and the information-matched supplement

Original baselines use `(x,c)`. Expanded baselines retain those inputs and
add categorical observation status `R` and continuous oxygen record `W`.
Observed W uses the training-calibration mean/SD; hidden W takes b=0,
with b=-1,+1 as prespecified sensitivities. This is an input expansion,
without an oxygen-imputation model or changes to native package kernels.

Class-only testing supplies no exact test oxygen. Matched mixed testing
reveals 20% or 50% under the saved masks, to EIV-GP and expanded baselines
alike. Both modes use the same fitted model. All responses in the test set
are withheld from fitting and tuning.

```{r prediction-report, eval=settings$action!="plan" && "prediction" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=11, fig.height=8}
ocean_show_predictions(analysis$prediction)
```

The O20/O50 comparisons use the prespecified primary expanded encoding b=0.
The original O0 baselines and calibrated expanded baselines are identified
in the table. Paper-ready CSV/Markdown/LaTeX/HTML tables are exported beside
the raw scores. Fold SD is descriptive variation
across the overlapping training sets, not an independent-replicate SE.

## 4. Oxygen imputation and response functions

These displays require the complete original paper fits and all continuations
selected from their current initial diagnostics. Partial fitting jobs can finish and report predictions
before this final component is available.

```{r diagnostics-build, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, include=FALSE}
diagnostics <- NULL
available <- analysis$prediction
if(is.null(available)) available <- ocean_prediction_report(output_dir,analysis$inputs,"paper",augmented_output_dir)
baseline_ready <- all(vapply(1:5,function(f) file.exists(file.path(output_dir,"full5_class4",sprintf("fold%02d",f),"baseline_package_outputs.rds")),logical(1)))
diagnostics_ready <- all(available$availability$available) && baseline_ready
diagnostic_run <- NULL
if(diagnostics_ready) diagnostic_run <- ocean_logged(file.path(output_dir,"jobs",settings$run_id,"diagnostics.log"),
  ocean_run_diagnostics(output_dir,data_dir,report_dir=diagnostics_dir,
    augmented_output_dir=augmented_output_dir, representative_fold=params$representative_fold,
    workers=params$diagnostics_workers,build_prediction=FALSE,prediction_report=available,
    build_surfaces="surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules))
if(!is.null(diagnostic_run)) diagnostics <- diagnostic_run$diagnostics
```

```{r diagnostics-display, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=13.2, fig.height=6}
if(is.null(diagnostics)) cat("Final U/m/f diagnostics are pending: complete the five original baseline tasks, all EIV cells, and their diagnostic-selected continuations.\n") else
  ocean_show_diagnostics(diagnostics,show_prediction=FALSE)
```

```{r diagnostic-appendix, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "diagnostics" %in% settings$modules && isTRUE(params$appendix), echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=13.2, fig.height=14}
if(!is.null(diagnostics)) {
  cat("\n\n### Separate fitted folds\n\n")
  print(diagnostics$plots$u_all_folds);print(diagnostics$plots$m_all_folds);print(diagnostics$plots$fm_all_folds)
  cat("\n\n### Class-specific imputation scores\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(ocean_paper_u_tables(diagnostics$u$summary)$class))
}
```

U imputation retains five metrics on the same 80 commonly hidden training
rows per fold. Its figure shows all training rows at O0/O20/O50, including
hollow calibration points. O0 stays on the model coordinate and has no raw-U
recovery score. Mean-function bands include conditional GP uncertainty and
exclude response noise; they differ from Y prediction intervals.

## 5. Response functions alongside measured profiles

The m comparison uses native `(x,c)` baseline predictors and EIV category
means on the same grid. EIV O0 supplies the comparison with class-only
training information; O20/O50 illustrate calibrated fits. An expanded
baseline slice at `(R=0,W=b)` is not automatically the population category
mean m, so it is not presented as that target.

```{r surfaces-build, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules, include=FALSE}
surfaces <- if(exists("diagnostic_run") && !is.null(diagnostic_run)) diagnostic_run$surfaces else NULL
surface_files <- file.path(diagnostics_dir,"tables",c("m_points.csv","f_points.csv"))
if(is.null(surfaces) && all(file.exists(surface_files)) && all(vapply(1:5,function(f)
  file.exists(file.path(output_dir,"full5_class4",sprintf("fold%02d",f),"baseline_package_outputs.rds")),logical(1))))
  surfaces <- ocean_surface_report(output_dir,data_dir,diagnostics_dir,representative_fold=params$representative_fold)
```

```{r surface-main, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules, echo=FALSE, results="asis", fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
if(is.null(surfaces)) cat("Surface displays are pending: run diagnostics and supply the original baseline fits.\n") else {
  print(surfaces$plots$m_comparison);print(surfaces$plots$f_with_observations)
}
```

```{r surface-appendix, eval=settings$action!="plan" && settings$profile=="paper" && "surface_comparison" %in% settings$modules && isTRUE(params$appendix), echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=13}
if(!is.null(surfaces)) {print(surfaces$plots$m_comparison_all_folds);print(surfaces$plots$f_with_observations_all_folds)}
```

For the pressure-slice m plot, the local salinity pool is divided
into six log-pressure bins over the fitted curve range, retaining at most
three nearest-salinity profiles per bin. This display rule uses inputs only;
the fitted grids and posterior calculations stay fixed. The same-X combined
plot adds the original baseline category means on its right panel.

Points are measured silicate at nearby profiles, with training/held-out
membership distinguished. Their salinity and pressure vary around the fixed
slice, and their responses include noise. They provide data context; they
are not true function values for calculating m/f recovery error. No true
response surface is available in this semi-real application.

## 6. Reproducibility

Task numbers and seeds do not depend on how work is divided. Completed-task
receipts and file hashes allow reuse and checked merging. Progress and full
logs are in `output_dir/jobs/run_id/`; predictions, native statuses, draws,
imputations, and derived figures remain in the result directory.

Data: GLODAPv2.2023 merged and adjusted product, DOI **10.25921/zyrq-ht66**.
Product reference: Lauvset et al. (2024), *Earth System Science Data* 16,
2047–2072, DOI **10.5194/essd-16-2047-2024**. See the bundled data README.
